Downstream request: [unbraind/pm-cli#1657](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1657), tracked in pm-cli as [pm-gh1657](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/main/.agents/pm/features/pm-gh1657.toon).

## Problem

Between pm-cli 2026.10.25 and 2026.10.30, seven changes altered observable SDK behaviour. Six were classified under **Fixed** and one under **Security**, because the generator buckets by type, resolution and title. None of the generated lines said that a caller contract changed or how to migrate. One Dependabot bump then broke 9 of 34 downstream extensions. Each one had to rediscover its cause by reading the pm-cli diff.

`--breaking-changes` does not cover this. It detects breaking signals, but these changes are fixes that also change a default, an error code, an ordering or a refusal. They need a migration line, not a breaking label.

## Proposal

1. pm-cli will let the closing item declare an observable contract change, with `before`, `after` and `migrate` text, through existing pm metadata. The exact field is decided on the pm-cli side, in pm-gh1657.
2. pm-changelog renders each declared change in a `### Changed (SDK contract)` section as `<title>: <before> → <after>. Migrate: <migrate>`. This applies even when the item would otherwise land in Fixed or Security, and that item does not appear twice.
3. `--changelog-json` exposes the same entries as structured records, for example `{ id, api, change, migrate }`, so Dependabot-driven fleets and agents can map a failing test to its cause.
4. `pm changelog audit` maps each contract line to its item, like every other generated line.

## Acceptance

- An item that declares a contract change renders once, under `Changed (SDK contract)`, with its migration line, in Markdown and JSON.
- Items without the declaration render exactly as today. Existing snapshots are unchanged.
- Audit maps the new lines and reports a declared change with no migration text as a gap.
